chunks: And from him, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Jamil ibn Darradj, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who divorced his wife, then left her until her waiting period expired, then married her again, then divorced her without having intercourse with her, and did this three times, he said: 'She is not permissible to him until she marries another husband.'

key_terms.دَخَلَ بِهَا: He had intercourse with her / consummated the marriage

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man divorces his wife three times without having intercourse with her?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that three pre-consummation divorces constitute a complete 'Taliq' (irrevocable divorce), rendering the wife permanently forbidden to the husband until she marries another man. This ruling is derived from the principle that each divorce, even without intercourse, counts towards the total of three, thereby requiring a new marriage contract (Nikah) rather than a simple re-marriage. The condition of 'Zawj Ghayruhu' (another husband) implies a genuine marriage with consummation, distinguishing it from the minor 'Taliq' where only one divorce occurred.
